**Landed:** `Network` (Embeddings section icon) → **`Zap`**, and the defaults groups gained the `entities` kind with **`ScanText`** (§22, 2026-09-14) · `connections.model` (the column) → **legacy mirror of the default
model**, with the model itself moving to `connection_models` and every selection
becoming an **(endpoint, model) pair** (0114) · `SourceKind` → **band** · `project()` → **toCandidate** · _arm_ →
**mechanism** · `role` (entries) → **field role**, in prose · `grant` (models) →
**lease** · `lane` (specs, retrieval) → **gather branch** / **mechanism** ·
`runtime` (plugins) → **sandbox** · `capability` (plugins) → **permission** ·
`ContextBlock` → **`Allocation`**, with assemble's `blocks` out-port → **`allocations`** ·
`koboldcpp_models` (table) → **`local_models`**, with `koboldCppModels` →
**`localModels`** and `Select`/`InsertKoboldCppModel` → **`…LocalModel`**.

⚠ **The vendor name was the only vendor-specific thing about that table.** It
already had what a registry needs — `filename` unique, provenance, a download
`status`, and a trust ordering on what it claims — and embedding and NER models
need exactly that. One concept, one table, one scan protocol. It gained `format`
and `modality`; it deliberately did **not** gain an `engine`, because a `.gguf`
is not KoboldCPP's and a stored engine would go stale the day a backend is added
(`enginesFor` derives it instead).

⚠ **`kind` was kept, not collapsed into `modality`**, and the two are not
synonyms. **`kind`** (`text` · `image` · `unknown`) is a _loader lane_ — which of
koboldcpp's two directories opens the file, which is what a GGUF header read can
actually answer. **`modality`** is the _role_, in the vocabulary above.
Collapsing them would make that header read record `text-gen` at `detected` —
the top of the automatic trust order — for a BERT `.gguf`, whose architecture is
a language model and whose modality is `embeddings`. That is manufacturing a
measurement, so instead **one function projects one onto the other**
(`modalityForKind`) and every write site goes through it, which is what stops
two columns that mean different things from coming to disagree.

⚠ **What the _allocation_ pass could not reach, and why.** The type renamed; two
fields did not, and neither is a rename this pass was free to make:

- **`AllocatedContext.blocks` is the SDK's word at a seam, not ours.** The object
  rides the `context` port into the SDK executor, and `isAllocatedContext` — an
  **exported** predicate, so a third-party node may call it — recognises an
  allocated context by `Array.isArray(v.blocks)` and nothing else. Renaming the
  field leaves `receipt.preview.blocks` and `preview.totals` silently empty on
  every run (verified against a real preview turn: populated before, `[]` after)
  and breaks the predicate for every plugin. R5 applies — translate at the seam,
  never merge — and the seam's word is the SDK's. ⚠ The deeper problem underneath
  it is not a rename either: `sdk/src/wire.ts` exports **its own** `ContextBlock`
  and `AllocatedContext`, a _different shape_ under the same names, which the
  app's object satisfies only by accident. That wants its own pass.
- **`meta.retrieval.blocks`** is derived from the field above and typed in the
  socket contract. Moving it alone would give one array two names on one path, so
  it moves when the field does.
- **`pipeline_blocks` was a third live sense**, and the only one with a table: a
  spec's `each` / `gather` / `loop` / `junction` containers. **Ruled 2026-09-15: it is a
  _clause_** (§4). The table, `BuiltClause.kind` and the builder verbs say `clause` /
  `gather` / `each` / `junction` since 2026-09-16 (plans/29 R-14, 30 §U3).

⚠ **What the _arm_ pass could not reach, and why.** Three things still spell it,
and none of the three is a rename:

- **`semantic.arm.*` and `names.arm.*`** are node keys, so they are _declared
  config addresses_. Moving one is a **cull** (§6): `reconcileConfigs`
  hard-deletes the value with a notice, and stale `pipeline_node_overrides` rows
  survive it and need a hand-written `DELETE`. Worth doing — as a migration.
- **`foundBy: "arm0#3"`** is a value written into receipts. Changing it changes
  what already-stored receipts say.
- **The retrieval-explain labels** — "Both arms", "One retrieval arm found it" —
  are prose a user reads, so they are free to change but are a copy change and
  not a rename (§24.6).

⚠ **`arm64` is not an instance of _arm_.** A whole-word search for `arm` returns
CPU-architecture strings in the tunnel binary manager, where `"arm64"` and
`"arm"` are values matched against `process.arch`. Renaming them breaks platform
detection on ARM machines, and it breaks it at _download_ time — the failure is a
wrong binary, not a type error. **Any mechanical `arm` pass must exclude
`tunnels/`.** Recorded because the residual count looks larger than it is: of the
hits outside tests, the architecture strings are a meaningful share and none of
them are this word.

⚠ **What the _runtime_ pass could not reach.** Two things, and neither is a
rename this pass was free to make:

- **`plugins/RuntimeManager.ts` still exists**, as a re-export of
  `SandboxManager` carrying a tombstone. Two files under
  `pipelines/runtime/` — `pluginBindings.ts` and `pluginBindings.int.test.ts` —
  still import the old name from the old path and belong to another lane's tree.
  The shim is one line and its removal is one line on each side of that seam.
- **QuickJS's own `runtime` is not ours.** `qjs.newRuntime()`, `JS_FreeRuntime`
  and the per-call VM object keep the library's word. R5: translate at the seam,
  never merge — a `sandbox.dispose()` that is really a WASM VM teardown would be
  the merge this rule exists to stop.

⚠ **The one _capability_ sense the permission pass left alone.** Where the word
names the **object-capability machinery** rather than a thing an admin may deny
— the _capability bridge_ (QuickJS's async host-function transport), the _abort
capability_, the SDK's `sp-capability-guard` — it stays. Those are not "what
sandboxed code may do"; they are how anything reaches it at all, and a
"permission bridge" that also carries ambient host functions would be a worse
name, not a better one. Everything permission-gated — network, storage,
resources, events, and every grant derived from them — now reads _permission_.

### Writing Room, manuscript, folio, scribe — 2026-09-17 (plans/genres §2, U2)

The co-writing genre and its vocabulary. Every word here was grepped before it
was used, and three of them are the genre's whole idea.

- **Writing Room** — the genre (`core:genre/writing-room`). Two words, title
  case in display text, the id hyphenated. Not _co-writing_ (a gerund, R4) and
  not _studio_ or _workshop_ (both already read as a place in the app's own
  vocabulary of panels).
- **manuscript** — the channel slug for the text being written. The book, never
  the session. Occurs nowhere else in the codebase.
- **folio** — the channel **role** whose messages fold into one block of prose.
  Landed with R-C the same day and is recorded here because this genre is its
  first user: _document_ was retired the day it landed (R1 — a _document_ is a
  pipeline's stored spec), and _folio_ is the distinctive word (R2).
- **scribe** — the genre's envoy key, and the companion's display name when no
  card is seated. `editor` was **REJECTED** (R-D): it already names the layout,
  style and CSS editors, and one word may not mean two things (R1). ⏳ The name
  and the placeholder glyph are the project owner's to set, as the guide's
  mascot's are.
- **family `writing`** — a new value of the open `family` string beside `chat`,
  `adventure` and `assistant`. A co-writing room is none of the three: nobody is
  playing anybody, there is no world, and the companion is not answering
  questions about the app.
- **`item.channel`** — a new published value on the message venue, beside
  `item.isNewest`. Which channel a row is on, so an action declared for one
  channel's messages can say so in an `enabled-when` predicate. Added because
  `venue.channel` — the declared way to say it — cannot be relied on yet: an
  action listing is built for ONE channel and the client asks for none.
- **the channel strip** — the composer's control for which channel the next
  message lands on. Not a _tab strip_: it does not switch panels, it switches
  where a message goes, and `docs/sessions.md` already used _tab strip_ for the
  composer's More panels.

Field names, all new and all read by a shipped prompt: **`pov`**, **`tense`**,
**`chunkLength`**, **`authorsNote`**. Action keys:
**`continue-manuscript`** (not bare `continue` — that is core's built-in verb,
R1), **`rewrite`**, **`expand`**, **`tighten`**, **`brainstorm`**,
**`critique`**, **`add-to-bible`**, **`export-manuscript`** (not bare `export`,
which names the character/lorebook card exports).

### plugin widget id — 2026-09-17 (ruled the same day)

A plugin's own widgets — the ones it declares under ⏳ `surfaces.panels`, which
belong to no genre — are now seated in every session, and they are seated under a
**plugin widget id**: `<pluginId>:<panelId>`, composed by the SDK's
**`pluginWidgetId`** and read back by **`parsePluginWidgetId`**
(`sdk/src/surfaces.ts`). The app composes it once, at the boundary where a
stored manifest is read (`frameHost.surfacesOf`), so every reader past that line
— `sessions:view.modePanels`, `session_panel_layouts`, `widget_settings`,
`widget_styles`, a `surface:open` intent — names one string.

- **plugin widget id** — R3-qualified, because the bare _widget id_ is what core
  and a genre use and those stay **plain**. Only a plugin's is qualified, and
  only because a package's panel id is the one id nobody else controls: two
  packages each picking `map` pick one widget id, and a layout row outlives the
  install that could have told them apart. `:` is the separator on the pattern
  of `core:genre/chat`, and it is unambiguous by grammar — the plugin slug
  (§23) admits no colon and neither does the panel-id grammar
  `^[a-z0-9_-]+$`.
  ⚠ Not a _panel id_: the panel id is the bare half the package declared, and it
  is what the ⏳ `sessions:view.panels` row still carries.
- **`enabledPluginWidgetIds(db)`** (`server/plugins/frameHost.ts`) — the one
  answer to "is this plugin widget id real?", read from the stored manifests
  through `surfacesOf`. `widgetStyles`'s `announcedWidgetIds` is its first
  reader.
- **`emitSurfaceIntent(…, pluginId?)`** — the emitting package's id, so a bare
  panel id it names is qualified server-side. A plugin may open its own widgets
  and nobody else's: an id prefixed with another plugin's is dropped (a drop,
  not a refusal — the whole verb is a proposal). Core and genre callers omit it
  and keep plain ids.

No migration, and nothing to migrate: no stored row has ever held a plugin panel
id, because they never mounted. `res.panels` is now explicitly ⏳ **remove at
0.7.0**. A disable deletes nothing — `sessions:view` simply stops listing the
plugin's widgets and the client draws them as missing, so a re-enable brings the
arrangement back. `announcedWidgetIds` refuses a NEW style for a disabled
plugin's widget while leaving the rows already made alone.

⚠ Two claims this falsified, both fixed in the same change: the
`FrameSurfaceDecl.settings` ⚠ in `sdk/src/surfaces.ts` said a `surfaces.panels`
declaration's settings never reach a frame (they do now — the genre loop in
`sessions:view` also never copied `p.settings`, so a genre's widget had the same
bug), and `userStyleSlug`'s uniqueness argument rested on "widget ids are
colon-free", which a plugin widget id is not. The argument survives on segment
count; the comment says so.

### contract · policy (of a definition) — 2026-09-17 (plans/31 V6, ruled the same day)

A node definition's content hash covers its **contract** — what a pinned spec
runs against — and nothing else; everything else on a `Descriptor` is
**policy**, what is offered or shown, stored on the registry row and never
hashed. _What is offered is policy; what runs is contract._ The SDK's
`definitionContract` / `definitionContractHash` compose and digest the
contract from a `Descriptor` or a `RegistryEntry` alike; the descriptor
registry's re-declaration guard and core's `pipeline_definition_registry`
pointer both call it, so the two answers to _is this the same definition?_
are one. `hash.ts` keeps its display denylist for every other registry.

- **contract (of a definition)** — §5. `DESCRIPTOR_CONTRACT_KEYS`. `review.fields`,
  `shape`, `earlyExit`, `liveRow`, `declaresRandomness` and `media` gained
  registry columns so a row read back reproduces its own pointer
  (`live_row`, `review`, `media`, and the existing `early_exit`,
  `declares_randomness`, `connection_kind`).
- **policy (of a definition)** — §5. `DESCRIPTOR_POLICY_KEYS`; `RegistryEntry.policy`
  and the `policy` jsonb column (migration 0150) carry `provisional ·
reviewDefault · timeoutMs · timeoutKind · toggleable`; `i18n` and `public`
  keep their own columns. `RegistryEntry.provisional` moved inside it.
- **provisional** — §5 amended: policy, not hashed. U6's "binding it
  republishes" is reversed; the row's `status` still derives from it.

Cost: every published definition republished once (112 pins in
`registryHashes.test.ts`; the id and version are contract and were never in
the material, so no pin could stay). Two definitions never share a hash now.
No spec document moves. The rename retry in `adoptCurrent` (0134) is gone:
a hash older than this build's material is kept beside the row as this
build reads it, never recomputed.

### one identity for an action — 2026-09-17 (plans/31 V2, ruled the same day)

An action had three keys: its `key`, its `function` (what routing resolved,
shareable across specs), and the identity `<spec slug>#<key>` the U5c passes
had already made the storage key. V2 keeps the identity alone. Bindings map
a **subject** — an identity, or a core event id for what core emits — to the
spec that serves it; a genre's enabled-when defaults, a session's override,
a preset's included set and the fire all key by identity; a slash name
means one action. _Function_ is retired (§23).

- **subject (of a binding)**, **binding (pipeline)** — §9, new rows.
  `pipeline_function_bindings` → **`pipeline_bindings`**, `function_key` →
  **`subject`** (migration 0151, a rename); pre-V2 rows re-keyed at boot
  (`boot/bindingSubjects.ts`: `respond` → `core:event/message-respond@1`, a
  bare key → its sole declarer, else dropped with a notice).
- **action** — §9 amended: the identity is the one key. `ActionDecl.function`
  is a one-release alias (`normalizeAction` reads it as `key`); `CORE_ACTIONS`
  are key-only; `GenreDecl.enabledWhen` is keyed by identity (`core#retry`,
  `core:spec/look#look`) and refuses a bare key; `slashCollisions` compares
  identities; a block's `fn` is the action's **key**.
- **slash name** — §9 amended: the same key under one name is a collision.
- SDK: `resolveFunctionVerdict/Spec` → **`resolveSubjectVerdict/Spec`**;
  `bindFunction` → **`bindSubject`**; `functionCandidates` →
  **`subjectCandidates`**; `EVENT_FOR_FUNCTION` deleted;
  `resolveSessionEventVerdict` gains the session's own binding as its first
  layer (the R-6 event half). Sockets: the **field** `function` retired for
  `action` / `key` (⏳ a bare key the door resolves) on `triggerFunction` and
  `setFunction`, `subject` on the binding pair; event names unchanged. The
  palette's `shared` row is gone with the alternatives it stood for.
- The `session_functions` bare-key fallback is retired (column name kept).
- ⚠ **R1 collision, pending the owner:** _binding_ now names both the cast
  link (§8) and the pipeline row (§9). Kept as the plan wrote it; flagged on
  both rows.

Cost: the compiled documents of every action spec lost one field, so the
Lair, Whodunit and Writing Room document pins moved once (their test files
record the old hashes). No definition hash moved.

### next-speaker strategy — 2026-09-21 (plans/19 §5 U-C5 closed; ruled the same day)

None of the genres' turn detection worked: the socket pre-picked every turn
with the 0.5 lookback rule, fed it to the run as an explicit pick, and every
strategy honours a pick — so the `speaker` node recorded the socket's guess,
the Turn order dropdown changed nothing, and planner-driven genres got a
character stamped on their narrator's placeholder row. Ruled: retire the
pre-pick and the column outright; plugins dictate the menu and may ship their
own detection as a script kind; round robin becomes once-per-turn-of-the-
person's.

- **next-speaker strategy** — §9, new row; **planner** amended.
- **group reply strategy** · **`nextSpeaker`** — §23, retired.
- SDK: `SessionShape.speakerStrategies` (replaces `nextSpeaker`);
  `PresetDefaults.speakerStrategy` (replaces `groupReplyStrategy`);
  `core:script:turn/select@1` (`turnSelect`, the `turn` content scope);
  `ctx.scripts.apply(point, value)` beside `applyText`; contracts
  `turnUserSplit` · `turnScripted`; respond, guide and writing-room specs
  seat `speaker` BEFORE `placeholder`, pinned `turnRoundRobin`, and the
  placeholder reads `$.speaker.*`.
- App: `runtime/speakerRotation.ts` (the rules, pure), `entities/speaker.ts`
  (`effectiveSpeakerStrategy` · `previewNextSpeaker` · `NEVER_DECIDES`),
  `speakerNodePin`, `listSpeakerStrategies(db, genreId?)`,
  `ReplyTurn { kind: 'respond' }` with nobody named, `ReplyOutcome.nobodyDue`,
  `sessions:triggerGenerateMessage.nobodyDue`, `sessions:speakerStrategies`
  by `genreId`, `sessions:create.session.speakerStrategy`,
  `GetResponseOrder.{known, speaker}`; migration 0152 (rebinds from the
  column, then drop); `getNextCharacterTurn.ts` and `GroupReplyStrategies.ts`
  deleted.

Cost: every respond/create document pin moved (the shape rides in them) and
the respond spec was edited in place under the freeze, content-addressed.
Three definition hashes added, none moved.

| **one primary row** / **one write per pipeline** (F7, F37, C21 — 09-B B4, R-17) | **one live row** per run (W1, owner R44 2026-09-23): the live row is a placeholder or claimed row, never a complete message; other writes, complete messages included, unlimited and allowed inside clauses; the live row never inside an `each`/`loop`; no second message on the live row's channel (validator for a literal channel, host `racesLiveRow` for a wired one). _Primary row_ survives only in comments on create → update pairs. |

## 26. Shell

The app-wide frame around every page (ruled 2026-09-15, built the same day). Vocabulary is
user-facing: these words appear in labels, docs and code alike.

| Term             | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **rail**         | The one navigation strip on the left edge. Its entries are **rail items**. ⚠ Not a _nav bar_, not a _sidebar_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **sidebar**      | The single 400px column beside the rail that shows one **sidebar view** at a time. There is one; "left/right sidebar" is retired.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **sidebar view** | What a rail item opens: Characters, Sampling, Admin… Code: `view`, `activeView`, `openViews`. ⚠ Never _panel_ — a panel is an area session widgets inhabit (§9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **detail**       | The read-only screen for one item inside a sidebar view, shown beside the list at desk width: "open the character's detail". Code keeps the legacy file names `*ViewPanel.svelte`; prose never says _panel_ here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **atmosphere**   | An animated background layer that paints with the theme's roles and sits under a screen's content: rain, snow, mist, glyph rain, a candle's glow. Code: `src/lib/client/atmospheres/`, ids `core:atmosphere/<slug>`, registry `ATMOSPHERES`, component `AtmosphereLayer`. Today only the login screen, one at random per load. ⚠ Not a _background_ (a session's image, §9) and not an _effect_ (pipeline kinds are effect classes, §4). A computed still scene, if built, is a **backdrop**, never an atmosphere. 🚧 Provisional until a second surface adopts it. |
| **tab**          | An opened sidebar view kept mounted while another shows; marked by a dot on its rail item. Not a UI tab strip.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **width**        | How wide a sidebar view is shown: **Dock** (the 400px sidebar, beside the page), **Half** (half the room right of the rail, beside the page; reached by dragging the view's **edge**, which snaps to Dock, Half or Focus) or **Focus** (over the page, which stays mounted). Code: `ViewWidth`, `panelsCtx.viewWidth` / `setViewWidth`, `shellPrefs.dockWidth` (which of Dock/Half a view comes back at), `fullPageView` (the view in Focus). Focus owns the view's **address** (`/characters`, `/lorebooks`…, `viewRoutes.ts`) through shallow routing, so Back steps down a width. Replaces _full page_ (2026-09-26). |
| **Jump**         | The one search: the **Jump pill** (top-right entry point), the **Jump overlay** (input + results), the **scope chip** (what it searches), **jump scope** (`view` / `route` / `manual`), and **jump kind** / **jump hit** (§25 ledger row). A **wire jump kind** is served by `jump:search`; a **client jump kind** (`doc`, ruled 2026-09-16) is produced by the client from data it already holds and never crosses the wire. One vocabulary, two producers.                                                                                                         |
| **wide rail**    | The rail with its **navigation titles** shown: 208px, the wordmark, a label per item, group names **Play** and **Tune**. Toggled by the user; `panelsCtx.railWide`, `localStorage serene-pub:railWide`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Library**      | The sidebar view that browses the community character library (`library`, `/library` in Focus) and imports into Characters. Characters only: there is no persona shelf. ⚠ Not the **pipeline library** (`/pipelines/library`), and not "your library" meaning the characters you have (§9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **bottom bar**   | The rail's form under the `lg` breakpoint: Home, Sessions, Characters, Lorebooks, Views.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Views sheet**  | The sheet the bottom bar's Views item opens: the open views first (a phone has no rail to carry their dots), then every other rail item. Code keeps `isMobileMenuOpen`. Replaces _More sheet_ (2026-09-26).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Activity**     | The sidebar view (rail item at the foot, Bell) that holds the person's **notifications** (§25, 2026-09-28) in three sections: **Waiting on you** (open rows), **In progress** (running and awaiting-review job cards), **Earlier** (cleared rows); administrators also get its **LLM queue** tab. Its rail dot is the worst level among UNREAD notifications (red `error`, gold `attention`; `info` lights none; a job card is never counted — a finished job raises its owner an `activity-ready` / `activity-failed` row, 2026-09-28, and counts through that), and on a phone the Views button carries the worse of the Activity and Admin dots, counts in its aria-label. `ActivitySidebar.svelte`. |
| **spine**        | The 56px strip on the right of a view in Focus over a session: the cast, an ember dot while a reply is being written, and the way back. On a phone it is the **return bar** at the top of a view's sheet. Only drawn when a page is underneath.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Stage only**   | Ctrl+. on desktop: the rail and the sidebar step aside so a session is its story and composer. `panelsCtx.stageOnly`; `data-stage-only` on the shell root is the flag a page reads to hide its own chrome. Esc leaves.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **folder**       | A user-made group of characters in the Characters sidebar view (ruled 2026-09-15): flat, no nesting, a character sits in one folder or none, a folder holds only characters. `character_folders` + `characters.folder_id`. ⚠ Not a **tag** (a tag is a many-to-many label); not the message model's container metaphor, whose schema comment now says _envelope_.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## 27. Documentation

The docs suite (ruled 2026-09-16, `~/.claude/plans/DESIGN-docs-suite.md`). One compiler, two
**profiles**, two hosts: pages are **rendered** at build time and both the app and
serenepub.com serve the rendered output. User-facing words appear in labels and the guides;
the rest is code.

| Term                 | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **docs compiler**    | `@serene-pub/docs`, a workspace in the SDK repo beside `cli`. Markdown in the **docs dialect** in, **docs-dist** out. Content-agnostic; knows nothing about the app. ⚠ Not a generator — a generator _emits_ markdown, the compiler _renders_ it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **docs dialect**     | Markdown plus the compiler's fences: highlighted code, `playground`, `:::note` / `:::tip` / `:::warning` admonitions, captioned figures with `{w=N}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **docs-dist**        | The compiler's output: `manifest.json`, `search.json`, `pages/<slug>.html`, converted assets. One per **docs profile**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **docs profile**     | Which sources one compile reads and where it writes them — `scripts/build-docs.js`, `buildDocs({ profile })`. Two: **app** (`app` + `sdk`, into `src/lib/generated/docs` + `static/docs/assets`, held to the page budget, the only one the Vite plugin builds) and **site** (`app` + `sdk` + `api`, into the gitignored `docs-site/`, `npm run docs:site`, copied whole by serenepub.com). ⚠ Not a **source** — a profile _selects_ sources. Qualify it: bare `profile` is already an image-generation profile schema and an evidence profile (§13).               |
| **guide**            | A hand-written page about the app (`docs/*.md`). The **source** `app`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **reference page**   | A page rendered from declarations — never hand-written. Two **sources**: `sdk` (the catalog, from a package's announcement, then the **laws**, from `@serene-pub/conformance`'s requirements) and `api` (the TypeDoc API reference, emitted by the SDK's own build into its gitignored `docs/generated/api`, slugged under `sdk/api`). Both carry the same banner and repo line. `api` is read by the **site** profile only — 2.4 MB of rendered HTML the app will not carry — and an unbuilt SDK checkout drops it with a warning rather than failing the compile. |
| **executed example** | An SDK example (`sdk-tests/examples/<slug>.example.ts`) whose source is shown verbatim, run at SDK build against the fixture host, and whose output is kept as a **golden** (§13). Built 2026-09-16; the app never runs one, it reads what the SDK build proved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **banner**           | The per-source notice the compiler prepends to every page of a source — today the SDK's "plugin modding is only available in 0.7 previews". Emitted by the build, never written by hand, so no page can forget it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **playground**       | The interactive SDK code runner embedded in a page (`@serene-pub/playground`, classic scripts, an opaque-origin `allow-scripts` frame). It _runs in_ a **sandbox** (§12); it is not one, and is never called one. Built 2026-09-16.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **nav group** · **order group** | A **nav group** is one heading of the docs nav (`DocsManifest.nav[]`, a source + a group name + its slugs). A source's `order` is flat (one nav group, headed by the source's `group`) or a list of **order groups** (`{ group, pages }`), each its own nav group, so the `app` source fills **Start here** · **Guides** · **How-to** · **For power users** · **Reference and help** while `docs/` stays flat. ⚠ The nav group **Guides** is a subset of the **guides**: every page of the `app` source is a guide, whichever group it sits in.                    |
| **Help**                        | The rail item (`BookOpen`, §22) that opens the documentation as a sidebar view; `/docs/<slug>` is its Focus address and Document View's `/document-view/docs` its mirror. Its search box and **Jump** (§26) share one query; a heading is a `doc` hit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Modder vocabulary

The words a modder learns first (R36: at most 25; more needs the owner). The SDK's
`guides/vocabulary.md` gives each one sentence, one example and a link back here, and
`guides/your-first-plugin.md` uses only these words, linking any other canon term where it first
appears. Each word's entry here carries **📘**. The guide never redefines a word: where the two
disagree, this file wins and the guide is fixed. `sdk-tests/vocabulary.test.ts` holds this list
and the guide's equal, checks each mark, and fails on an unlinked canon term in the first-plugin
guide.

- **plugin** — §12.
- **genre** — §9.
- **spec** — §4.
- **node** — §4.
- **inlet** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **query** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **task** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **oracle** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **outlet** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **port** — §4.
- **node definition** — §5.
- **handler** — §4.
- **pin** — §9, under **swap**.
- **swap** — §9.
- **receipt** — §4.
- **event** — no entry of its own yet. The sense a modder means (an occurrence in a session,
  core's `core:event/…` or one a package declared and a write recorded) is stated in passing
  under **action** (§9) and in the custom-events row of §25.
- **action** — §9.
- **declared setting** — §9.
- **annex** — §9.
- **turn order** — §9.
- **turn strategy** — §9, under **turn pool** · **turn orderer** · **turn strategy**.
- **widget** — §9.
- **component** — §9.
- **host element** — §9.
- **conformance** — no entry of its own yet. The kit's words are in §25 (_package conformance
  words_, 2026-09-26) and under **verdict** (§4).
